name: Lightsheet 7

specs.Immersion: works at refractive indices 1.33-1.58 (ECi, iDISCO, CLARITY, PEGASOS, EasyIndex and others)
specs.Illumination: Pivot Scanner swings the sheet angle to reduce shadow stripes
specs.Environment: heating, cooling and CO2 for live samples
specs.Example: 13.1 x 13.1 x 6 mm cleared brain volume in about 40 min (4x4 tiles, 866 planes)

summary: Multiview light-sheet microscope with separate illumination and detection optics, used both for live embryos and for large cleared organs. It accepts clearing media across a wide refractive-index range and mounts samples vertically in a chamber.

sources.title: ZEISS Lightsheet 7 product page

name: Lattice Lightsheet 7

specs.Light sheet: lattice pattern generated with a spatial light modulator and dithered
specs.Sample carriers: standard slides, 35 mm dishes, chamber slides and multiwell plates with No. 1.5 coverslip bottoms
specs.Environment: temperature, CO2, O2 and humidity control for hours-to-days imaging

summary: Commercial lattice light-sheet microscope that images through the coverslip of ordinary sample carriers instead of requiring a dipping-objective geometry. It aims at long-term, low-phototoxicity volumetric imaging of living cells and small organisms.

sources.title: ZEISS Lattice Lightsheet 7 product page

name: MuVi SPIM

specs.Optics: 2 illumination and 2 detection objectives, horizontal geometry
specs.Field of view: 299-1664 um (LS), 333-5990 um (CS), depending on objective and zoom
specs.Versions: LS for live samples, CS for cleared samples (exchangeable optical unit)

summary: Multiview light-sheet microscope with two illumination and two detection arms, so two opposing views are recorded without rotating the sample. It descends from the MuVi-SPIM design published by the Hufnagel lab at EMBL in 2012.

sources.title: Bruker MuVi SPIM family page
Krzic et al. 2012, Multiview light-sheet microscope for rapid in toto imaging, Nat Methods

name: InVi SPIM Lattice Pro

specs.Objectives: detection Nikon CFI Apo 25x/1.1 W; illumination 28.6x/0.7 W
specs.Magnification: 31.3x (208 nm pixels, 426 um FOV) or 62.5x (104 nm pixels, 213 um FOV)
specs.Light sheets: static sheet, scanned Gaussian, scanned Bessel, optical lattices
specs.Speed: 80 fps full frame, up to 500 fps on a reduced field
specs.Geometry: inverted, open top, V-shaped sample holder

summary: Inverted, open-top light-sheet microscope with one illumination and one detection objective looking up into a V-shaped sample holder. It can switch between Gaussian, Bessel and lattice light sheets for live and fixed samples.

sources.title: Bruker InVi SPIM family page
Bruker light-sheet technology details

name: TruLive3D Imager

specs.Optics: 2 illumination and 1 detection objective, inverted open-top geometry
specs.Environment: integrated environmental chamber for long-term live imaging

summary: Inverted light-sheet system with dual-sided illumination built for long-term live imaging of delicate specimens such as organoids, stem cells and small embryos. Samples sit in an open-top V-shaped holder, allowing several samples per experiment.

sources.title: Bruker launches Luxendo TruLive3D Imager (News-Medical, Dec 2019)
Bruker light-sheet technology details

name: LCS SPIM

specs.Optics: 2 illumination and 1 detection objective, inverted open-top geometry

summary: Inverted light-sheet microscope for large cleared specimens, which are placed in quartz cuvettes of up to 10 cm length above the optics.

sources.title: Bruker light-sheet technology details
Bruker InVi SPIM family page (comparison table)

name: UltraMicroscope Blaze

specs.Light sheets: 1-6 sheets, illumination from one or both sides
specs.Automation: automated objective and zoom changes, autofocus, multi-sample chamber

summary: Automated light-sheet microscope for large chemically cleared samples, up to a whole cleared mouse, with motorized objective and zoom changes. It descends from the LaVision ultramicroscope line.

sources.title: Miltenyi Biotec launches fully automated light sheet microscope (Technology Networks, May 2020)
Emory ICI core: Miltenyi Blaze LFOV light sheet

name: UltraMicroscope II

specs.Example configuration: 2x/0.5 MVPLAPO objective with dipping cap, sCMOS camera, sheet NA 0.1, 3 um z-steps (Renier et al. 2016)

summary: Horizontal-sheet light-sheet microscope for cleared tissue that grew out of the ultramicroscopy work of Dodt and colleagues. It became a common instrument for whole-brain imaging with iDISCO-type clearing and the ClearMap pipeline.

sources.title: Renier et al. 2016, Mapping of brain activity by automated volume analysis of immediate early genes, Cell
Dodt et al. 2007, Ultramicroscopy, Nat Methods

name: TCS SP8 DLS

specs.Design: TwinFlect mirror deflects the scanned illumination beam by 90 degrees to form the sheet

summary: Digital light-sheet option for the TCS SP8 confocal: a TwinFlect mirror turns the scanned laser beam by 90 degrees so that one instrument can image in both confocal and light-sheet modes.

sources.title: Leica TCS SP8 DLS product page (archived)

name: Viventis LS2 Live

specs.Illumination: two Nikon 10x/0.2 objectives, three switchable sheets of about 2, 3 and 7 um FWHM
specs.Detection: two Nikon 25x/1.1 water objectives, 590 um field, 260 nm pixels
specs.Sample holder: open-top multiwell chambers with media exchange

summary: Open-top light-sheet microscope with dual illumination and dual detection for long time-lapse imaging of organoids and embryos in multiwell chambers. Leica lists it as archived and replaced by the Viventis Deep.

sources.title: Leica Viventis LS2 Live product page (archived)
UZH ZMB: Viventis LS2 Irchel

name: Viventis Deep

specs.Design: dual illumination, dual-view detection, open-top multiwell holders
specs.Cleared samples: up to 9 x 6 x 6 mm with user-replaceable detection optics
specs.Options: photomanipulation arm, media exchange during time-lapse

summary: Successor to the LS2 Live: a dual-view, open-top light-sheet microscope for multi-position live imaging of organoids and embryos, whose detection optics can be swapped for cleared samples.

sources.title: Leica Viventis Deep product page
Babraham Institute imaging facility: light-sheet microscopy

name: Lattice LightSheet
summary: Commercial version of the original Janelia lattice light-sheet design, sold by 3i under a ZEISS sublicence from December 2014 as a development system while ZEISS worked on its own turnkey instrument.

sources.title: ZEISS sublicenses lattice light sheet microscopy to 3i (Cambridge Network, Dec 2014)

name: diSPIM / iSPIM

resolution.note: isotropic, after fusing the two views (diSPIM)

specs.Geometry: two perpendicular water-dipping objectives above an inverted stand; views alternate and are fused
specs.Speed: up to 200 images (2-10 volumes) per second
specs.Supply: ASI stages, galvos and piezos; objectives, lasers and cameras sourced separately

summary: Inverted light-sheet head with two objectives at 45 degrees above a coverslip, developed with Hari Shroff's lab at NIH. Alternating which objective illuminates and which detects gives two views that are fused into an isotropic volume.

sources.title: ASI diSPIM / iSPIM product page

name: SmartSPIM

specs.Light sheet: axially swept, synchronized with the camera rolling shutter
specs.Speed: 20 fps; mouse brain hemisphere in under 30 min at 1.8 x 1.8 x 4 um voxels

summary: Axially swept light-sheet microscope for large cleared samples, from organoids to rat brains and juvenile mice. Sweeping the sheet focus with the rolling shutter keeps axial resolution uniform across the field.

sources.title: LifeCanvas SmartSPIM product page

name: Aurora 3D (3Di)

specs.NA: collection up to 0.7, illumination up to 0.06

summary: Hybrid open-top light-sheet microscope for cleared tissue that first scans the whole specimen at low resolution and then zooms in on chosen regions. The hybrid open-top architecture comes from academic work by Glaser, Liu and colleagues.

sources.title: Alpenglow Biosciences 3Di hybrid open-top light-sheet microscope
Glaser et al. 2022, A hybrid open-top light-sheet microscope, Nat Methods

name: Multiphoton Mesoscope

resolution.note: 2p-RAM design values at field centre, 970 nm excitation, NA 0.6

summary: Commercial two-photon mesoscope built under licence from HHMI on the Janelia two-photon random-access mesoscope (2p-RAM) design. It gives cellular resolution across a 5 mm field, enough to cover several cortical areas at once.
applications: calcium imaging across cortical areas in mice

sources.title: Janelia: 2-Photon Random Access Mesoscope
Laser Focus World: Mesoscope provides 100X imaging volume

name: nVista
summary: Head-mounted one-photon fluorescence miniscope for calcium imaging in freely moving rodents, recording at 25 frames per second across a field of under 1 mm. Specs listed are for the V2 microscope.
applications: calcium imaging in freely behaving mice

sources.title: Inscopix support: nVista microscope specifications

name: nVoke

specs.Field of view: 600 x 900 um, shared by imaging and stimulation

summary: Miniscope that combines calcium imaging with optogenetic stimulation through the same head-mounted microscope. Imaging and stimulation use separate blue and red-orange bands so that, for example, GCaMP can be recorded while red-shifted opsins are driven.
applications: all-optical recording and manipulation of neural circuits in behaving mice

sources.title: optics.org: Inscopix launches nVoke (Nov 2016)

name: nVista 2P
summary: Head-mounted two-photon miniscope for single-cell calcium imaging in freely behaving animals, sold as a complete system with laser and acquisition hardware. It works with cranial windows and GRIN lenses.
applications: two-photon calcium imaging in freely moving mice

sources.title: Bruker introduces nVista 2P miniature microscope (News-Medical, Apr 2025)
Inscopix nVista 2P system page

name: Fluorescence miniscopes (Snap-in and Twist-on)

specs.Surface models (-S): SFMB-S one colour, OSFM-S imaging plus optogenetics, 2CFM-S two colour, through a cranial window
specs.Deep-brain models (-L): GRIN lens in an imaging cannula; 2CFM-L two-colour with two CMOS sensors
specs.Electronic focus: eFocus models with 300 um focus range

summary: Family of head-mounted one-photon miniscopes for surface and deep-brain calcium imaging, with one-colour, two-colour and imaging-plus-optogenetics variants.
applications: calcium imaging in freely moving rodents

sources.title: Doric Lenses: Miniature microscopy solutions

name: NeuraLight 3D Ultra

specs.Hardware: liquid-crystal spatial light modulator with a larger chip than earlier NeuraLight 3D
specs.Platform: port module for Ultima 2Pplus and selected Ultima microscopes made since 2006

summary: Holographic photostimulation module for Bruker Ultima two-photon microscopes. A spatial light modulator shapes the stimulation laser into many 3D target spots so chosen neurons can be activated optogenetically while the network is imaged.
applications: all-optical interrogation of neural circuits in vivo

sources.title: Bruker introduces NeuraLight 3D Ultra (News-Medical, Jun 2022)

name: Mesolens

resolution.note: measured FWHM, widefield mode (confocal: 800 nm and 8 um)

specs.Volume: specimens up to 6 mm wide and 3 mm thick

summary: Large custom objective that pairs low magnification with high numerical aperture, so a 6 mm field is imaged at sub-micron lateral resolution. It was used to image whole fixed mouse embryos in a single field.

sources.title: McConnell et al. 2016, A novel optical microscope for imaging large embryos and tissue volumes, eLife

name: Slit ultramicroscope

specs.Illumination: convergent beam from the side, observation at 90 degrees
specs.Detection: scattered light from particles; 4 nm gold particles sized in cranberry glass

summary: Instrument in which a beam of light enters a colloid from the side and particles are viewed through a microscope at right angles, so only scattered light is seen. With sunlight it revealed gold nanoparticles a few nanometres in size and is the earliest ancestor of side-illuminated light-sheet microscopy.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ultramicroscope

name: OPFOS
manufacturer: Voie, Burns and Spelman (University of Washington)

resolution.note: within a 1.5 mm field of view, cleared cochlea

summary: Orthogonal-plane fluorescence optical sectioning: a thin sheet of laser light crosses a cleared specimen at right angles to the viewing axis, giving optical sections of a whole excised guinea-pig cochlea. It is often regarded as the first light-sheet fluorescence microscope of the modern era.

sources.title: Voie et al. 1993, Orthogonal-plane fluorescence optical sectioning, J Microsc

name: SPIM
summary: Selective plane illumination microscopy combines a static sheet of light with orthogonal camera detection to image living samples up to a few millimetres with little photodamage. It showed muscles in live medaka and the embryogenesis of Drosophila.

sources.title: Huisken et al. 2004, Optical sectioning deep inside live embryos by SPIM, Science

name: DSLM
summary: Digital scanned laser light-sheet microscopy builds the sheet by rapidly scanning a thin beam, and was used to follow nearly every nucleus in zebrafish embryos over the first 24 hours of development. The result was a public 'digital embryo' of cell positions, divisions and tracks.

sources.title: Keller et al. 2008, Reconstruction of zebrafish early embryonic development by scanned light sheet microscopy, Science

name: MuVi-SPIM
summary: Multiview SPIM with two illumination and two detection objectives in a fixed arrangement, so opposing views are recorded together and fused in real time. It imaged whole Drosophila embryos with subcellular resolution and was later commercialized by Luxendo.

sources.title: Krzic et al. 2012, Multiview light-sheet microscope for rapid in toto imaging, Nat Methods

name: SiMView
summary: Light-sheet microscope with four synchronized optical arms that records multiple views of an embryo at once, with one-photon and two-photon versions. It followed cell dynamics across entire Drosophila embryos and traced neuroblast lineages.

sources.title: Tomer et al. 2012, Simultaneous multiview light-sheet microscopy, Nat Methods

name: Whole-brain light-sheet calcium imaging

specs.Volume rate: 0.8 Hz for the whole larval brain

summary: Light-sheet microscope used to record GCaMP5G activity from the whole brain of larval zebrafish, capturing more than 80% of neurons at single-cell resolution.

sources.title: Ahrens et al. 2013, Whole-brain functional imaging at cellular resolution using light-sheet microscopy, Nat Methods

name: IsoView
summary: Isotropic multiview light-sheet microscope that illuminates and detects along four orthogonal directions at once and deconvolves the views into one volume with similar resolution in all axes. It recorded whole-animal neural activity in Drosophila larvae for hours.

sources.title: Chhetri et al. 2015, Whole-animal functional and developmental imaging with isotropic spatial resolution, Nat Methods

name: Bessel beam plane illumination

specs.Speed: up to nearly 200 planes per second

summary: Scanned Bessel beams, combined with structured illumination or two-photon excitation, make light sheets thinner than 0.5 um for 3D imaging of single living cells. It was the direct forerunner of lattice light-sheet microscopy.
applications: mitochondria, filopodia and chromosome dynamics in live cells

sources.title: Planchon et al. 2011, Rapid three-dimensional isotropic imaging of living cells using Bessel beam plane illumination, Nat Methods

name: Lattice light-sheet microscope
summary: Ultrathin light sheets made from two-dimensional optical lattices image 3D dynamics for hundreds of volumes, often at sub-second intervals, at or beyond the diffraction limit. Demonstrations ranged from single transcription-factor molecules to C. elegans and Drosophila embryos.

sources.title: Chen et al. 2014, Lattice light-sheet microscopy, Science

name: Adaptive-optical lattice light-sheet microscope (AO-LLSM)
summary: Combines lattice light-sheet microscopy with adaptive optics to image subcellular processes without aberrations deep inside multicellular organisms. It showed endocytosis, organelle remodeling and cell migration inside zebrafish and other animals.
applications: immune and cancer cell migration in vivo

sources.title: Liu et al. 2018, Observing the cell in its native state, Science

name: Guide-star adaptive optics
summary: Adaptive optics using a descanned, laser-induced fluorescent guide star and direct wavefront sensing, correcting aberrations at high NA with a 14 ms update rate. It recovered diffraction-limited imaging over volumes more than 240 um on a side in the zebrafish brain.

sources.title: Wang et al. 2014, Rapid adaptive optical recovery of optimal resolution over large volumes, Nat Methods

name: Pupil-segmentation adaptive optics
summary: Adaptive optics method that illuminates sub-regions of the objective pupil one at a time and measures the resulting image shifts to work out the aberration. Applied to two-photon microscopy, it restored near-diffraction-limited imaging at depths of 400 um in fixed brain slices.
applications: deep two-photon imaging in brain tissue

sources.title: Ji et al. 2010, Adaptive optics via pupil segmentation for high-resolution imaging in biological tissues, Nat Methods

name: Oblique plane microscope (OPM)
summary: First oblique plane microscope: a single high-NA objective both creates an inclined light sheet and collects the light, and secondary optics re-image the tilted plane onto a camera. It removed the need for two orthogonal objectives around the sample.
applications: proof of principle on pollen grains

sources.title: Dunsby 2008, Optically sectioned imaging by oblique plane microscopy, Opt Express

name: SCAPE
summary: Swept confocally-aligned planar excitation microscopy uses an oblique light sheet swept through the sample by one objective, with descanning optics mapping the moving plane onto a fixed camera. It imaged neuronal activity in awake mouse brain and freely crawling Drosophila larvae at more than 20 volumes per second.

sources.title: Bouchard et al. 2015, Swept confocally-aligned planar excitation (SCAPE) microscopy, Nat Photonics

name: SCAPE 2.0
summary: Redesigned SCAPE with a high-speed intensified camera that reaches over 300 volumes per second and pixel rates above 1.2 GHz. It imaged freely moving C. elegans and blood flow and calcium in the beating zebrafish heart, and also cleared and expanded samples.

sources.title: Voleti et al. 2019, Real-time volumetric microscopy of in vivo dynamics and large-scale samples with SCAPE 2.0, Nat Methods

name: diSPIM
summary: Dual-view plane illumination microscope with two perpendicular objectives that swap illumination and detection roles; fusing the two views gives isotropic resolution. It followed nuclei through 14 h of nematode embryogenesis.

sources.title: Wu et al. 2013, Spatially isotropic four-dimensional imaging with dual-view plane illumination microscopy, Nat Biotechnol

name: Ultramicroscope for cleared brains
manufacturer: Dodt lab (TU Vienna / Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry)
summary: Adapted the side-illuminated 'ultramicroscopy' idea to whole fixed mouse brains made transparent by clearing, resolving single GFP-labelled neurons and dendritic spines.

sources.title: Dodt et al. 2007, Ultramicroscopy: three-dimensional visualization of neuronal networks in the whole mouse brain, Nat Methods

name: Open-top light-sheet microscope (OTLS)
summary: Light-sheet microscope with the optics underneath a flat sample plate, built for slide-free, non-destructive pathology of large clinical specimens. It examined surgical margins at about 12.5 s per square centimetre and cleared core-needle biopsies in 3D.

sources.title: Glaser et al. 2017, Light-sheet microscopy for slide-free non-destructive pathology of large clinical specimens, Nat Biomed Eng

name: ctASLM

resolution.note: best axial resolution, depending on configuration

summary: Cleared-tissue axially swept light-sheet microscopy sweeps a thin sheet focus across the field in step with the camera rolling shutter, giving isotropic subcellular resolution over millimetre-scale cleared samples in many immersion media.

sources.title: Chakraborty et al. 2019, Light-sheet microscopy of cleared tissues with isotropic, subcellular resolution, Nat Methods

name: mesoSPIM
manufacturer: mesoSPIM initiative (Helmchen lab, University of Zurich, and partners)

specs.Light sheet: scanned Gaussian beam, NA 0.15, axially swept with the rolling shutter

summary: Open-hardware axially scanned light-sheet microscope for centimetre-sized cleared samples such as a whole mouse central nervous system, with near-isotropic resolution and acquisition in minutes. Build plans and control software are shared openly.
applications: cleared mouse brain and spinal cord

sources.title: Voigt et al. 2019, The mesoSPIM initiative, Nat Methods
mesoSPIM features

name: OpenSPIM
manufacturer: OpenSPIM project (Tomancak lab, MPI-CBG, and partners)
summary: Open-access SPIM platform built from off-the-shelf and 3D-printed parts and run with Micro-Manager and Fiji. The sample hangs in agarose in front of the detection lens and can be rotated for multiview imaging.

sources.title: Pitrone et al. 2013, OpenSPIM: an open-access light-sheet microscopy platform, Nat Methods
OpenSPIM website

name: UCLA Miniscope V4
summary: Open-source head-mounted one-photon miniscope for calcium imaging in freely behaving animals, with an electronically adjustable focus.
applications: calcium imaging in freely moving mice

sources.title: Aharoni Lab: Miniscope-v4 repository
UCLA Miniscope Project knowledge base

name: Integrated miniature fluorescence microscope
summary: A 1.9 g fluorescence microscope built from mass-producible parts, including an LED light source and a CMOS sensor, that is carried on the head of a mouse. It tracked calcium spiking in more than 200 cerebellar Purkinje cells during locomotion.

sources.title: Ghosh et al. 2011, Miniaturized integration of a fluorescence microscope, Nat Methods

name: MINI2P
summary: Miniature two-photon microscope weighing under 3 g with an enlarged field of view and a fast tunable lens for multiplane imaging. It recorded more than 1,000 neurons at a time, and over 10,000 per animal, in freely moving mice.
applications: visual cortex, entorhinal cortex and hippocampus in moving mice

sources.title: Zong et al. 2022, Large-scale two-photon calcium imaging in freely moving mice, Cell

name: Light-field microscope for neural activity
manufacturer: Vaziri and Boyden labs (IMP Vienna / MIT)

specs.Volume: about 700 x 700 x 200 um at 20 Hz

summary: Light-field microscope with a microlens array that records a whole volume in each camera frame, then reconstructs it computationally. It imaged neuronal activity across an entire C. elegans and the larval zebrafish brain at single-neuron resolution.

sources.title: Prevedel et al. 2014, Simultaneous whole-animal 3D imaging of neuronal activity using light-field microscopy, Nat Methods

name: Two-photon random access mesoscope (2p-RAM)

resolution.note: field centre, 970 nm excitation (0.89 / 6.88 um at 2.5 mm off-centre)

specs.Example rates: four 600 x 600 um regions at 9.6 Hz; 4.4 x 4.2 mm at 1.9 Hz

summary: Two-photon mesoscope with a 5 mm field and subcellular resolution, whose scanners jump quickly between regions anywhere in the field. It imaged several widely separated cortical regions in behaving mice; Thorlabs sells a commercial version.

sources.title: Sofroniew et al. 2016, A large field of view two-photon mesoscope with subcellular resolution for in vivo imaging, eLife
Janelia: 2-Photon Random Access Mesoscope

name: Diesel2p

specs.Field of view: about 25 mm2, spanning distances up to 7 mm

summary: Open-source two-photon mesoscope with two independent scan engines that can image two separate regions of a large field at the same time. It combines optical design, adaptive optics and temporal multiplexing.
applications: calcium imaging of distributed cortical circuits

sources.title: Yu et al. 2021, Diesel2p mesoscope with dual independent scan engines, Nat Commun
